analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: For AI capex, forget about Congress and focus on state and local governments
key_insights: BofA argues state and local elections matter more than congressional elections for the AI capex cycle, because most immediate constraints on data center construction sit outside Washington.
Neither party is likely to hold a veto-proof Senate majority, which limits what Congress can do to regulate the AI buildout.

State and local governments have already enacted measures to slow data center construction, and are expected to play a larger role than the federal government in data center regulation and incentives.
The investment cycle will face a growing patchwork of state and local rules. BofA says this won't stop the capex cycle but could slow its pace and raise its cost.
BofA's 3Q 2026 GDP tracking estimate rose one tenth to 3.5% q/q saar after September construction spending, against BofA's official 3Q GDP forecast of 3.4%.
Today's data releases are factory orders, JOLTS job openings and total vehicle sales.
